title: Patient Counseling | Travelers' Health | CDC
content: Skip directly to site content Skip directly to page options Skip directly to A-Z link Skip directly to A-Z link Skip directly to A-Z link Patient Counseling Before Travel Resources CDC Yellow Book : Health Information for International Travel contains the US government's most current travel health guidelines, including pre-travel vaccine recommendations, destination-specific health advice, and easy-to-reference maps, tables, and charts. Vaccine Information Destination Pages Travel Vaccine Quick Guide Routine Immunization Schedules Vaccine Information Statements (VIS) Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book) Vaccine Administration (Pink Book) Vaccination Records Staying Up to Date with Your Vaccine Records Keeping Track of Records Patient Care Tools Pre-Travel Quick Guide : Highlights topics to discuss with patients traveling abroad. Destination Pages: Find travel health recommendations by country. Find a Clinic : Links to places you can get vaccines and medicine before you travel, including local health departments, travel medicine clinics, or yellow fever vaccination clinics. Factsheets for Travelers : One page information sheets for travelers with special needs and information for different types of travel. Disease Resources Countries & Territories at Risk for Zika : Check if Zika is a concern at a particular destination. Yellow Fever & Malaria Information by Country : Country-specific yellow fever vaccine requirements and recommendations and malaria transmission information and prophylaxis recommendations. Travel Health Notices: Get the latest country-specific information on disease outbreaks, special events or gatherings, and natural disasters affecting travelers' health. Clinical Updates After Travel Resources Patient Symptom Evaluation Tools Post-Travel Evaluation of the Ill Traveler : Most travel infections become apparent soon after travel, but incubation periods vary, and some syndromes can present months to years after infection. When evaluating a patient with a probable travel-related illness, the clinician should consider the items summarized below. Destination Pages : Provide vaccine preventable and other diseases that should be considered in a recent traveler who is ill. Screening Asymptomatic Travelers Post-Travel Respiratory Infections Post-Travel Diarrhea Post-Travel Dermatologic Conditions Post-Travel Parasitic Disease Including Evaluation of Eosinophilia Post-Travel Evaluation to Rule Out Viral Special Pathogen Infection Contact Us CDC Contact Information for Clinicians : Contact information for CDC assistance and information about infectious diseases. The American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene provides a list of physicians who offer clinical consultative service in Tropical Medicine, Medical Parasitology and Travelers' Health.
